title: Multiple transitions joining the same states overlap on state diagrams
author: peterc
body:
This is not something that I expect to be fixed quickly, but something I encountered. I suspect it is also true of the upstream project.

If you have a state diagram where two states refer to each other with multiple transitions, the edges get rendered over the top of each other. For example: 

```
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> Running : start
    Running --> Idle : stop
```

```
┌─────────┐
│         │
│         │
│         │
└────┬────┘
     │
     │
     │
     │
     ▼
┌─────────┐
│         │
│   Idle  │
│         │
└────┬────┘
     ▲
     │
   stopt
     │
     ▼
┌────┴────┐
│         │
│ Running │
│         │
└─────────┘
```

OG Mermaid renders the two edges with curved routing to avoid this overlap.

I'm going to have a try at fixing it, but this issue is here for anyone else who encounters it and may also want to fix. If I achieve anything, I'll comment or, potentially, drop a PR.

comments.author: balintorosz
comments.body:
Fixed in [v1.0.0](https://github.com/lukilabs/beautiful-mermaid/releases/tag/v1.0.0).

The ELK.js layout engine now routes parallel edges between the same nodes as separate paths with distinct label positions. The `start` and `stop` transitions between Idle and Running render as two clearly separated edges.

You can verify on the live demo: https://agents.craft.do/mermaid

title: Inconsistent rendering of flowchart branches  with -- Yes -->
body:
**Description:**
I am encountering an issue where some Mermaid flowcharts with labeled branches do not render correctly in my environment, Inconsistent rendering of flowchart branches with -- |Yes| --> 

**Content 1 (does not render as expected):**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A(Start) --> B{Is it sunny?}
  B -- Yes --> C[Go to the park]
  B -- No --> D[Stay indoors]
  C --> E[Finish]
  D --> E
```

**Content 2 (renders as expected):**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A{Is it raining?} -->|Yes| B{Have umbrella?}
  A -->|No| C([Go outside])
  B -->|Yes| D([Go with umbrella])
  B -->|No| E{Is it heavy?}
  E -->|Yes| F([Stay inside])
  E -->|No| G([Run for it])
```

**Additional information:**
- The only difference is the use of branch label syntax: content 1 uses `-- |Yes| -->`, content 2 uses `-->|Yes|`.
- Both diagrams render correctly on [mermaid.live](https://mermaid.live/), but not in my current deployment/environment.
- Mermaid version: [fill in]
- Rendering method: [e.g. extension, markdown parser, etc.]

**Expected:**
Both syntaxes for labeled branches should render consistently, as shown on mermaid.live.

**Actual:**
Content 1 fails to render, while content 2 works.

**Request:**
Please clarify whether both branch label syntaxes are officially supported and ensure consistent rendering across different environments.

comments.author: balintorosz
comments.body:
Fixed in v1.1.0 via PR #49. The parser now supports both label syntaxes:
- Pipe syntax: `-->|Yes|` ✅ (already worked)
- Text-embedded: `-- Yes -->` ✅ (now supported)

Also supports dotted (`-. Maybe .->`) and thick (`== Sure ==>`) variants.

Thanks for reporting this, @1119302165!

comments.author: dfadler
comments.body:
@1119302165 Heads up — this is fixed in our fork, [zombie-mermaid](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid), a maintained fork of beautiful-mermaid. Text-embedded edge-label syntax (`-- Yes -->`, `-. Maybe .->`, `== Sure ==>`) is now parsed correctly as a fallback alongside the pipe (`-->|Yes|`) form.

Fixed by [PR #49](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/49), commit [`9d722cf`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/9d722cf38012056f46810e6c0f32a85ab8cb084f), shipped in [v1.1.0](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/releases/tag/v1.1.0).

title: A* pathfinding in edge-bundling exhausts memory (Map maximum size exceeded) on dense TD graphs
author: ktrysmt
body:
## Bug `renderMermaidASCII` throws `RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded` on dense top-down flowcharts with multiple fan-in edge bundles. ### Reproduction ```ts import { renderMermaidASCII } from 'beautiful-mermaid'; const code = `graph TD A["AAA
(keita)"] --> C["CCC"] B["BBB
(yuriko)"] --> C C --> D["DDDD"] D --> E["EEEE"] A1["1 / 2"] --> A A2["3 / 4"] --> A A3["5 / 6"] --> A A4["XXX
(YYY ZZZ)"] --> A B1["77 77
(7 / 7 / 7)"] --> B B2["88-88
(99 99)"] --> B B3["111s 222s"] --> B D --> F{"F?"} F -->|Yes| G["High level
Tr"] F -->|No| H["Dumb Tr
S"]`; renderMermaidASCII(code); // => RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded ``` ### Stack trace ``` RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded at Map.set () at getPath (dist/index.js) // src/ascii/pathfinder.ts:164 at routeBundledEdges (dist/index.js) // src/ascii/edge-bundling.ts:277 at processBundles (dist/index.js) // src/ascii/edge-bundling.ts:326 at createMapping (dist/index.js) // src/ascii/grid.ts:537 ``` ### Analysis The diagram has 13 nodes and 15 edges forming three edge bundles: - **Fan-in to A**: A1, A2, A3, A4 (4 unlabelled edges) - **Fan-in to B**: B1, B2, B3 (3 unlabelled edges) - **Fan-out from D**: D -> E, D -> F (2 unlabelled edges) `routeBundledEdges` computes a junction point via `calculateJunctionPoint` and then calls `getPath` to route from each source's exit cell to the junction. On this graph, the junction point or its neighbors can become enclosed by other nodes' 3x3 grid blocks, making it unreachable through free cells. The root cause is in `getPath` (`src/ascii/pathfinder.ts:121-173`): 1. **No upper-bound check on grid coordinates.** `isFreeInGrid` (line 112) rejects negative coordinates but imposes no positive limit. The search space is unbounded in the +x/+y direction. 2. **No iteration limit.** When the destination is unreachable, A\* expands every reachable free cell in the semi-infinite positive quadrant until V8's `Map` size limit (~16.7M entries) is hit. ### Suggested fix Add a maximum iteration guard to `getPath`. When exceeded, return `null` (no path found) — the caller already handles this gracefully by falling back to a straight-line segment: ```ts // src/ascii/pathfinder.ts — getPath() const MAX_ITERATIONS = 50_000 export function getPath( grid: Map, from: GridCoord, to: GridCoord, ): GridCoord[] | null { const pq = new MinHeap() pq.push({ coord: from, priority: 0 }) const costSoFar = new Map() costSoFar.set(gridKey(from), 0) const cameFrom = new Map() cameFrom.set(gridKey(from), null) let iterations = 0 // + while (pq.length > 0) { if (++iterations > MAX_ITERATIONS) { // + return null // + } // + // ... rest unchanged } return null } ``` An alternative / complementary approach would be to clamp the search area to a bounding box derived from the grid's occupied extent (e.g., `max occupied coordinate + margin`). ### Environment - beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 - Node.js v25.8.1 / Linux

comments.author: dfadler
comments.body:
@ktrysmt Heads up — this is fixed in our fork, [zombie-mermaid](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid), a maintained fork of beautiful-mermaid. The ASCII/Unicode A* pathfinder is now bounded by a render-wide iteration budget (not just per-call), and unobstructed edges skip A* entirely and take a direct route, so dense graphs no longer exhaust the heap.

Fixed by [PR #89](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/pull/89), commit [`5fa08d0`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/5fa08d02245ff53ac113e29af71ca009c16635a9), shipped in [v1.2.0](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/releases/tag/v1.2.0).

comments.author: dynaum
comments.body:
Another trigger for the same error, with no edge bundles at all: a plain linear chain of 25 edges.

```ts
import { renderMermaidASCII } from "beautiful-mermaid";

const chain = (n: number) =>
  "flowchart TD\n" + Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => `  N${i} --> N${i + 1}`).join("\n");

renderMermaidASCII(chain(24)); // ~0.08 s, renders
renderMermaidASCII(chain(25)); // ~12 s, then RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded
```

Measured on beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3, Node 22, Apple M-series:

| Edges in the chain | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.07 s | renders |
| 24 | 0.08 s | renders |
| 25 | 12.5 s | `RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded` |

`flowchart LR` behaves the same. A fan of 30 edges from one node, two parallel chains of 12 and 13, and a 40-message sequence diagram all render in under 0.1 s, so the cliff seems tied to chain depth.

The 12 s before the throw hurts more than the throw. Terminal viewers that call a renderer with a timeout (herdr-file-viewer kills it at 5 s) lose the whole document's rendering. In [maidog](https://github.com/dynaum/maidog) I now draw in a child process with a deadline as a workaround.

comments.author: dfadler
comments.body:
🤖 **Claude** (posted on behalf of @dfadler)

@dynaum thanks for the extra trigger and the timing table, the 12 s before the throw is a useful detail.

I tried your `chain(n)` generator for n = 24, 25, 40 and 60 in both `TD` and `LR` against [zombie-mermaid](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid) (a fork of beautiful-mermaid, which I maintain) 5.0.1. All render without an error. I also ran the same generator against upstream 1.1.3 and reproduced your failure: the 25-edge TD chain threw `RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded` after 18.7 s (LR: 20.2 s), versus about 5 ms on the fork. I haven't bisected, so I can't say which change made the difference.

If you want to try it in maidog, `renderMermaidASCII` is the same entry point under the package name `zombie-mermaid`. If you still see a slow or failing case on it, a repro would be welcome as an issue on the fork.

comments.author: dfadler
comments.body:
🤖 **Claude** (posted on behalf of @dfadler)

Follow-up to my earlier comment: I bisected between upstream 1.1.3 and zombie-mermaid `main` on the 25-edge `TD` chain, so I can now say what changed.

The first fixed commit is [`bc455262`](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid/commit/bc455262db45e5a82f97f3a1a6cd9f2edf7ee5aa) in the fork, a port of #66 (thanks @ktrysmt). `getPath()` in `src/ascii/pathfinder.ts` counts iterations of the A* loop and returns `null` past `MAX_ITERATIONS = 50_000`. Callers already treat `null` as "no path", so the edge falls back instead of the open set and `cameFrom` growing until `RangeError: Map maximum size exceeded`.

On my machine (Node 22, single runs): the parent of that commit still hit my 30 s kill timer, and `bc455262` renders the chain in 74 ms. So #66 looks like it covers this trigger as well as the dense fan-in graph it was written for. I only tested the plain chain, not the edge-bundle cases from the original report.

it) makes it finish in ~25 ms; a pure iteration cap would also work.

title: Root detection in grid layout is order-dependent, misclassifying child nodes as roots
author: ktrysmt
body:
## Bug

`createMapping` misidentifies root nodes when edges defining `child → parent` relationships appear after `parent → grandchild` edges in the mermaid source. This causes all misidentified roots to be placed on the same grid level, producing a flat horizontal layout instead of the expected hierarchical tree.

### Reproduction

```ts
import { renderMermaidASCII } from 'beautiful-mermaid';

const result = renderMermaidASCII(`graph TD
    A["Parent A"] --> C["Child C"]
    B["Parent B"] --> C
    C --> D["Grandchild D"]
    A1["Root 1"] --> A
    A2["Root 2"] --> A
    A3["Root 3"] --> A
    B1["Root 4"] --> B
    B2["Root 5"] --> B`);

console.log(result);
```

**Expected:** A1, A2, A3, B1, B2 at the top level; A, B one level below; C, D below that.

**Actual:** A, B, A1, A2, A3, B1, B2 are all placed on the same row (level 0), producing a flat horizontal strip instead of a tree.

### Analysis

The root detection in `src/ascii/grid.ts:398-410`:

```typescript
const nodesFound = new Set<string>()
const initialRoots: AsciiNode[] = []

for (const node of graph.nodes) {
  if (!nodesFound.has(node.name)) {
    initialRoots.push(node)
  }
  nodesFound.add(node.name)
  for (const child of getChildren(graph, node)) {
    nodesFound.add(child.name)
  }
}
```

The comment says _"Identify root nodes -- nodes that aren't the target of any edge"_, but the implementation does not check all edge targets. It performs a single forward pass over `graph.nodes` (in Map insertion order from the parser) and marks a node as root if it hasn't been seen as a **child** yet.

The parser inserts nodes into the Map in the order they first appear in edges. So for:

```
A --> C       ← A inserted first
...
A1 --> A      ← A1 inserted after A
```

When the loop reaches node `A`, `A1 → A` hasn't been processed yet, so `A` has never been seen as anyone's child. `A` is incorrectly added to `initialRoots`.

The second filter (line 415-429) only removes subgraph nodes with external incoming edges — it does not catch this case for non-subgraph nodes.

### Suggested fix

Replace the order-dependent heuristic with a direct edge-target check:

```typescript
// Collect all nodes that are the target of at least one edge
const edgeTargets = new Set(graph.edges.map(e => e.to.name))

// Root nodes are those that never appear as an edge target
const rootNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => !edgeTargets.has(n.name))
```

This produces the correct result regardless of node insertion order.

For the reproduction case above:
- Current algorithm: `initialRoots = [A, B, A1, A2, A3, B1, B2]` (7 roots, **wrong**)
- Proposed fix: `rootNodes = [A1, A2, A3, B1, B2]` (5 roots, **correct**)

### Environment

- beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3
- Node.js v25.8.1 / Linux

Root detection is now a two-pass, order-independent algorithm (collect every edge target first, then anything never targeted is a root), so a `child --> parent` edge appearing before `parent --> grandchild` in source no longer misclassifies nodes as roots.

title: Root nodes in fan-in groups are placed without target-aware grouping, causing edge overlap
author: ktrysmt
body:
## Bug

When a graph has multiple fan-in groups feeding into different target nodes, all root nodes are placed in a flat horizontal sequence regardless of which target they connect to. This causes edge paths from different fan-in groups to overlap, making the diagram hard to read.

### Reproduction

```mermaid
graph TD
    A1 --> A
    A2 --> A
    B1 --> B
    B2 --> B
    A --> C
    B --> C
```

```ts
import { renderMermaidASCII } from 'beautiful-mermaid';

const code = `graph TD
    A1 --> A
    A2 --> A
    B1 --> B
    B2 --> B
    A --> C
    B --> C`;

console.log(renderMermaidASCII(code));
```

### Current output (conceptual)

```
A1   A2   B1   B2      <-- all roots on one row, no grouping
 └────┼────┴────┘       <-- paths overlap, can't tell A-group from B-group
      |    |
      A    B
```

### Expected output (conceptual)

```
A1   A2        B1   B2
 └────┘         └────┘
      |              |
      A              B
```

Root nodes feeding into the same target should be placed contiguously, with fan-in targets aligned near their respective root groups.

## Analysis

The root cause is in `createMapping` in `src/ascii/grid.ts` (around lines 448-455). Root nodes are placed sequentially with a fixed `+4` increment, without considering which downstream target each root feeds into:

```typescript
for (const node of externalRootNodes) {
  const requested: GridCoord = dir === 'LR'
    ? { x: 0, y: highestPositionPerLevel[0]\! }
    : { x: highestPositionPerLevel[0]\!, y: 0 }
  reserveSpotInGrid(graph, graph.nodes[node.index]\!, requested)
  highestPositionPerLevel[0] = highestPositionPerLevel[0]\! + 4
}
```

For the example above, A1, A2, B1, B2 all get placed at x = 0, 4, 8, 12 regardless of A being at one position and B at another.

Additionally, the child placement loop places children at the next available slot on their level (`highestPositionPerLevel[childLevel]`), ignoring the parent's perpendicular position. This means fan-in targets like B end up far from their root group (e.g. B1 at x=8, B2 at x=12, but B at x=4).

This also contributes to the pathfinding cost described in #64 — when roots are poorly positioned relative to their targets, edge routing becomes unnecessarily complex.

## Suggested fix

Two changes in `src/ascii/grid.ts`:

1. **Group roots by immediate downstream target** before placement. Roots feeding into the same target are placed contiguously, so their edge spans don't interleave with other groups.

2. **Align fan-in targets with their parents.** When placing a child that has multiple incoming edges (in-degree > 1), use `Math.max(levelTracker, parentPerpendicular)` instead of just the level tracker. This keeps fan-in targets near their root groups rather than at the next available slot.

### Edge cases to consider

- A root node with edges to multiple targets should only appear once (group by first child as a heuristic)
- Single fan-in group: no grouping effect needed, behavior unchanged from current
- LR direction: the same issue exists vertically; the fix should apply symmetrically

## Environment

- beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3

Fan-in root nodes are now grouped by their shared downstream target before grid placement, so nodes feeding the same target are placed contiguously instead of interleaved with unrelated roots.

title: TD/TB Flowchart Layout Flipping to Horizontal
author: jiezhengj
body:
## Problem Description

When rendering a flowchart with `flowchart TD` (Top-Down) or `flowchart TB` (Top-Bottom) that contains many backward/reverse edges (e.g., `C3 --> C1`), the layout incorrectly flips to a horizontal orientation instead of maintaining the specified vertical orientation.

### Expected Behavior

The diagram should render vertically (height > width) when using `TD` or `TB` direction.

### Actual Behavior

The diagram renders horizontally with a very wide aspect ratio (width ≈ 5.6x height).

## Reproduction Steps

1. Use the following Mermaid code:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[用户输入任务指令] --> B[目标深度解构：穿透商业本质，拆解可量化核心指标]

    C2 --> C3[洞察报告合规性与有效性校验]
    C3 -->|校验通过| D[模块2：非遗IP与内容策划]
    C3 -->|校验不通过| C1
    D --> D1[基于洞察结论筛选适配非遗项目]
    D1 --> D2[IP打造、年轻化表达与商业化路径设计]
    D2 --> D3[非遗内容合规性校验与授权规范确认]

    D3 -->|校验不通过| D1
    E --> E1[基于IP内容与客群洞察，拆分8周4阶段执行节奏]
    E1 --> E2[线下场景、线上玩法、分层客群活动细化]
    E2 --> E3[执行节点、落地标准与人员架构明确]
    E3 --> E4[活动方案与IP内容、预算约束交叉适配校验]
    E4 -->|校验通过| F[模块4：商业运营与成本管控]
    E4 -->|校验不通过| E1
    F --> F1[商户合作体系、招商方案设计]
    F1 --> F2[全周期成本明细拆分、营收预估与ROI测算]
    F2 --> F3[预算管控机制设计，总预算锁定780万内]
    F3 --> F4[成本方案与活动策划方案双向适配校验]
    F4 -->|校验通过| G[模块5：全渠道传播与舆情管理]
    F4 -->|校验不通过| F1
    G --> G1[匹配活动节奏，制定全周期传播策略与话题矩阵]
    G1 --> G2[分层KOL/KOC投放矩阵设计与效果管控]
    G2 --> G3[7*24h舆情监测体系与三级危机预案制定]
    G3 --> G4[传播方案与IP合规要求、活动节点双向对齐校验]
    G4 -->|校验通过| H[模块6：全案合规与风险防控]
    G4 -->|校验不通过| G1
    H --> H1[全案全模块合规性终审，设置一票否决权]
    H1 --> H2[全场景风险点识别、分级与应对预案制定]
    H2 --> H3[问题内容识别与退回修改]
    H3 -->|修改闭环| I[模块7：全案整合与定稿]
    H3 -->|校验不通过| C & D & E & F & G
    I --> I1[全模块内容整合，解决冲突与矛盾]
    I1 --> I2[全周期执行timeline与落地标准表制定]
    I2 --> I3[全案与核心目标、硬性约束最终校验]
    I3 -->|校验通过| J[最终可落地完整全案交付]
    I3 -->|校验不通过| I1
```

1. Render with beautiful-mermaid
2. Observe the layout is horizontal instead of vertical

## Root Cause

The ELK.js layout engine, when processing graphs with many backward edges (cycles), can incorrectly choose a horizontal layout orientation even when a vertical direction (DOWN) is explicitly specified. The default ELK configuration doesn't enforce the direction strongly enough for complex cyclic graphs.

## Solution

Add specific ELK layout options to force the correct vertical orientation and prevent layout flipping:

### File: `src/layout-engine.ts`

Add the following layout options to the root ELK graph configuration (around line 213-218):

```typescript
// Force correct direction and prevent layout from flipping
'elk.layered.cycleBreaking.strategy': 'DEPTH_FIRST',
'elk.layered.layering.strategy': 'LONGEST_PATH',
'elk.layered.crossingMinimization.strategy': 'LAYER_SWEEP',
'elk.layered.crossingMinimization.forceNodeModelOrder': 'true',
'elk.layered.crossingMinimization.semiInteractive': 'false',
```

### What these options do:

1. **`cycleBreaking.strategy: 'DEPTH_FIRST'`** - Uses depth-first cycle breaking which preserves the original direction better
2. **`layering.strategy: 'LONGEST_PATH'`** - Uses longest path layering which maintains the intended vertical flow
3. **`crossingMinimization.forceNodeModelOrder: 'true'`** - Forces nodes to stay in their original definition order
4. **`crossingMinimization.semiInteractive: 'false'`** - Disables semi-interactive mode which could reorder nodes

## Results Before Fix

- Width: 3662.35 px
- Height: 650.30 px
- Aspect Ratio: 5.63:1 (very wide, horizontal)

## Results After Fix

- Width: 983.93 px
- Height: 3372.70 px
- Aspect Ratio: 0.29:1 (tall, vertical - correct!) ✅

The diagram now properly renders in the vertical TD/TB orientation as specified.

title: Sibling edges from the same source fail to share a trunk segment (ASCII)
author: rmvegasm
body:
## Sibling edges from the same source fail to share a trunk segment

### Description

When multiple edges originate from the same node with the same exit direction, they should share a common trunk segment before branching to their targets. Instead, each edge independently routes from the source, producing disconnected paths where later edges take unnecessary detours instead of following the first edge's trunk.

### Reproduction

Render the following Mermaid diagram:

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Src["Source"]
    Left["Left Target"]
    Center["Center Target"]
    Right["Right Target"]
    Src -->|left*| Left
    Src -->|center*| Center
    Src -->|right*| Right
```

### Actual behavior

The Right edge detours to y=2 instead of sharing the y=1 horizontal trunk with the Center edge. The labels for center\* and right\* land on the wrong segments:

```
│    Source   ├────/center*──────┐
│             │          │       │
└──────┬──────┘          └───────┼───────/right*───────────────┐
       │                         │                             │
    /left*                       │                             │
       ▼                         ▼                             ▼
```

### Expected behavior

All three edges share a common trunk from Source's right border. Each label sits on its own vertical branch:

```
│    Source   ├─────────────┬─────────────────────┐
│             │             │                     │
└──────┬──────┘          center*               right*
       │                    │                     │
     left*                  │                     │
       ▼                    ▼                     ▼
```

### Root cause

The A* pathfinder runs independently for each edge. When two candidate paths have equal Manhattan cost, the min-heap's LIFO tie-breaking (`<` in `sinkDown`) picks the wrong alternative. Additionally, old branch items from early A* expansion stay in the queue and are explored before more direct items from later expansion — preventing sibling edges from naturally converging on the same trunk.

### Proposed approach

1. Make the min-heap tie-breaking deterministic (FIFO via `<=` in `sinkDown`)
2. Order MOVE_DIRS exploration so each edge's initial exit direction is explored first (Right for TD Right-exit edges, Down for LR Down-exit edges)
3. Add post-processing in the grid layout that re-routes subsequent sibling edges from the first edge's branch point (where it turns toward its target) instead of from the source, with explicit T-junction character drawing at convergence points

title: Box-start connector (`├`) displaced from the source box border when a sibling edge has a label (ASCII)
author: rmvegasm
body:
## Box-start connector (`├`) displaced from the source box border when a sibling edge has a label

### Description

The box-start junction character — `├` for Right-exit edges, `┤` for Left-exit, `┬` for Down-exit, `┴` for Up-exit — is placed at a position derived from `gridToDrawingCoord` on the edge's start grid cell. This returns the center of that grid cell. When a sibling edge's label widens the column (to accommodate its label text), the cell center shifts right, and the connector follows — even though the actual box border hasn't moved.

### Reproduction

Render the following Mermaid diagram:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Src["Source"]
  Top["Top Target"]
  Mid["Middle Target"]
  Bot["Bottom Target"]
  Src -->|top*| Top
  Src -->|mid*| Mid
  Src -->|bot*| Bot
```

### Actual behavior

The `├` for the Top edge floats 2–3 characters right of Source's right border. The Mid edge's label (`/mid*`) is placed on horizontal segment `(1,5)→(4,5)`, which causes `determineLabelLine` to widen column 2 (the Source node's right border column) from 1 to 7 character widths. This shifts `gridToDrawingCoord` for the Top edge's start cell, which `drawBoxStart` uses to place the connector:

```
┌────────┐             ┌───────────────┐
│        │             │               │
│ Source │  ├──/top*──►│   Top Target  │
│        │             │               │
└────┬───┘             └───────────────┘
           ^^^
           ├ should be flush on the │
```

### Expected behavior

The `├` sits directly on Source's right border, replacing the `│` character at the box edge:

```
┌────────┐        ┌───────────────┐
│        │        │               │
│ Source ├─/top*─►│   Top Target  │
│        │        │               │
└────┬───┘        └───────────────┘
```

### Root cause

`drawBoxStart` computes the connector position as `firstLine[0].x - 1`, where `firstLine[0]` comes from `drawLine` with `offsetFrom=1` applied to `gridToDrawingCoord`. The coordinate chain is:

```
Mid edge's label widens col[2] (Source's border column)
  → gridToDrawingCoord(2,1).x = col[0] + col[1] + floor(col[2]/2)
  → returns 12 instead of 9
  → drawBoxStart places ├ at 12 instead of 9
```

The box border itself hasn't moved (it's defined by `col[0] + col[1]`, independent of the widened border column `col[2]`), but the connector placement logic doesn't use the box border — it uses the shifted grid-cell center.

### Proposed approach

Replace the grid-cell-center derivation with a direct box-border computation via `getNodeAttachmentPoint` (a function that already exists and is used by bundled edges). Pass this coordinate to both `drawPath` (as the first segment's start override) and `drawBoxStart` (for the junction character placement), so the line and the connector start from the actual box border regardless of column-width changes from other edges' labels.

title: Bug: marker-start arrowheads missing on bidirectional (<-->) and backward (<-.-) SVG edges
author: wsnark
body: ## Summary Every start-side arrowhead (`marker-start`) is missing in SVG output. Bidirectional edges (`<-->`) render with only the end/target head, and backward edges (`<-.-`) render with **no head at all** — just a bare line. Forward (`-->`) edges are unaffected. ## Environment - `beautiful-mermaid` `1.1.3` (current `main`) - Reproduced in librsvg (`rsvg-convert`), Inkscape, and Firefox. ## Reproduction ```ts // Repro: start-side arrowheads (marker-start) are missing on backward `<-.-` // and bidirectional `<-->` flowchart edges — the line renders but the head does not. // // Cause: the `arrowhead-start` marker is double-reversed — orient="auto-start-reverse" // (already a 180° flip) is combined with a pre-reversed polygon, so the head points // into the line and vanishes in librsvg / Inkscape / browsers. The bug lives in two // marker generators, so we emit two SVGs: default markers, and linkStyle-colored ones. // // Run: bun run repro.ts import { renderMermaidSVG } from 'beautiful-mermaid' import { writeFileSync } from 'node:fs' const graph = `graph TD Top <--> Bot Top <-.- Bot` // Cosmetic only, unrelated to the bug: beautiful-mermaid colors everything via CSS // var(--…); viewers that don't resolve custom properties would show black boxes, so // flatten to plain black-on-white (fills → white, strokes/text/arrows → black). const view = (svg: string) => svg.replace(/var\(--(_node-fill|bg)\)/g, 'white').replace(/var\(--[\w-]+\)/g, 'black') writeFileSync('repro.svg', view(renderMermaidSVG(graph))) writeFileSync('repro-color.svg', view(renderMermaidSVG(`${graph} linkStyle default stroke:#2563eb`))) ``` Run `bun run repro.ts`, then open `repro.svg` (default markers) and `repro-color.svg` (the `linkStyle`-colored variant). ## Expected vs. actual - **Expected:** the `<-->` edge has a head at *both* ends; the `<-.-` edge has a head pointing back into `Top`. - **Actual:** the `<-->` edge has a head only at `Bot`; the `<-.-` edge has no head at all. **Before (buggy) / after (fixed):** ## Root cause The `arrowhead-start` marker is *double-reversed*. In `src/renderer.ts`: ``` ``` `orient="auto-start-reverse"` already rotates the head 180° to point back out of the start node — but the polygon is *also* pre-reversed (tip at `x=0` instead of `x=8`). The two reversals cancel, so the head points **into** the line and vanishes. The forward `arrowhead` marker uses `orient="auto"` with the non-reversed polygon, which is why end heads render fine. Both marker generators are affected: `arrowMarkerDefs()` and `arrowMarkerDefsForColor()` (the latter for `linkStyle` stroke overrides). ## Fix Reuse the forward head's geometry for the start marker (non-reversed polygon + matching `refX`), keeping `orient="auto-start-reverse"` for the single intended flip. PR incoming. ## Related Same underlying bug as #58 (open since 2026-03, appears stalled). This report adds a reproducer, root cause, and fix. ## Separate minor note The parser only accepts `<` before a complete op (`-->`, `-.->`, `==>`, `---`, `-.-`, `===`), so `A <-- B` and `A <== B` are silently dropped as edges. Not addressed by this fix.

title: Flowchart: `~~~` invisible edges are ignored, and per-subgraph `direction` leaks diagram-wide
author: brandonburrus
body:
### Summary

Two related flowchart layout defects around subgraph layout control, found while rendering diagrams through [`rsgdev`](https://github.com/RepublicServicesRepository/rsgdev) (an internal CLI that bundles `beautiful-mermaid@1.1.3` for Mermaid rendering):

1. **`~~~` invisible ordering edges are not handled at all.** Grepping the built `dist/index.js` for `~~~` returns zero matches — there's no parsing or layout handling for this standard Mermaid.js edge type, which is normally used to pin node order without drawing a visible connector.
2. **A `direction` statement nested inside a `subgraph ... end` block is parsed but not scoped to that subgraph.** The parser does capture it (`subgraphStack[subgraphStack.length - 1].direction = ...`), but the layout engine appears to apply it diagram-wide instead of only to the subgraph's own contents.

### Repro 1 — `~~~` ordering edges ignored

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph Row1
    R1[Node 1]
    R2[Node 2]
    R3[Node 3]
    R1 ~~~ R2 ~~~ R3
  end
```

- **Expected:** R1, R2, R3 ordered left-to-right per the invisible-edge chain (matches Mermaid.js / mermaid.live).
- **Actual:** node order is unaffected by the `~~~` edges.

### Repro 2 — subgraph `direction` leaks diagram-wide

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph Row1
    direction LR
    A1 --> A2 --> A3
  end
  subgraph Row2
    direction LR
    B1 --> B2 --> B3
  end
  subgraph Row3
    direction LR
    C1 --> C2 --> C3
  end
```

- **Expected:** each subgraph's own contents laid out left-to-right, while the three subgraphs stack top-to-bottom per the outer `flowchart TB`.
- **Actual:** the entire diagram renders as a single, very wide, short row — the `LR` direction leaks out of the subgraphs and applies diagram-wide instead of staying scoped.

### Environment

- `beautiful-mermaid`: `1.1.3` (exact resolved version, via `node_modules/beautiful-mermaid/package.json`)

### Possibly related

#138 also shows incorrect nested-subgraph layout (duplicated content, random ordering) with a similar nested `direction` construct, though the failure mode described there (rendering duplication/overflow) looks different from the diagram-wide leak described here. Filing separately since they don't obviously share a root cause, but flagging in case a fix ends up touching the same code path.

### Workaround

Detect these two constructs in flowchart source and fall back to a real Mermaid.js renderer (e.g. `@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli`) for affected diagrams, which handles both correctly.

title: ASCII: vertical edge lines draw through spaces in edge labels
author: NahumLitvin
body:
```
graph TD
  A -->|push = build| B
```

renders as

```
  push =│build
```

The line shows through the space in the label. Single-word labels look fine only because there's no space to leak through.

Cause: `mergeCanvases` treats every space in an overlay as transparent (`src/ascii/canvas.ts:246`, `if (c !== ' ')`), and the label canvas from `drawTextOnLine` (`src/ascii/draw.ts:677`) is merged that way, so a label's spaces never cover the path under them.

Possible fix: write label spaces as a placeholder (a non-breaking space, say) in `drawTextOnLine` so the merge keeps them, then map it back to a plain space when the canvas becomes a string. Happy to send a PR if that direction works for you.

Seen with 1.1.3 (latest on npm).

comments.author: dfadler
comments.body:
@NahumLitvin Beautiful Mermaid doesn't look to be maintained anymore, so I wanted to say this is fixed in [zombie-mermaid](https://github.com/dfadler/zombie-mermaid), a maintained fork. The vertical edge label now sits beside the stroke instead of the line cutting through its spaces. This came with the broader "label beside the stroke" change rather than a targeted fix.

Mermaid source:

```mermaid
graph TD
  A -->|push = build| B
```

title: Class diagrams: superclass is aligned with one subclass instead of centered over them
author: ajlakanen
body:
A superclass with several subclasses ends up above one of them, often an outer one, so inheritance trees look lopsided.

```mermaid
classDiagram
  Animal <|-- Dog
  Animal <|-- Cat
  Animal <|-- Bird
```

With 1.1.3 the box centers are Animal 130, Bird 100, Dog 260, Cat 420. Written the other way round (`Dog --|> Animal` …) Animal is centered, so the
result depends on edge direction.

Flowcharts already pass `'elk.layered.nodePlacement.bk.fixedAlignment': 'BALANCED'` (`src/layout-engine.ts`), but `buildClassElkGraph` in `src/class/layout.ts` does not, so ELK picks the narrowest of its four Brandes–Köpf alignments. Adding the same option puts Animal at 260.

Suggested change (`src/class/layout.ts`, `layoutOptions`):

```ts
'elk.layered.nodePlacement.bk.fixedAlignment': 'BALANCED',
```

Notes from trying it on diagrams with uneven widths, deep trees, multiple inheritance, edge labels, cycles and disconnected parts:

- Equally wide subclasses: superclass exactly centered. With very uneven   widths it sits above the middle subclass instead, which is how Brandes–Köpf works; still much better than the edge.
- No new overlaps, edge crossings, or edges through boxes.
- Size is mostly unchanged; a deep skewed tree grew from 380 to 440 px, since the default picks the narrowest alignment.
- `NETWORK_SIMPLEX` placement gives the same positions but wider diagrams.
